alicia: Quick update from the quant ablation runs on rf-7b-v2 against prod_holdout today. Tried three configs: full-FP, MLP-INT8 (attention FP16), and ATT-INT8 (MLP FP16).
david: nice. headline metrics?
alicia: NDCG@10 / MRR@10 relative to full-FP:
  - MLP-INT8: NDCG@10 -1.5% (paired p=0.03), MRR@10 +0.6% (p=0.14)
  - ATT-INT8: NDCG@10 -0.9% (p=0.08), MRR@10 +0.2% (p=0.4)
fiona: so MLP quant hurts NDCG more than attention quant, but both give tiny MRR upticks. Are drops concentrated in any slice?
alicia: yes - short-query (<=5 tokens) accounts for ~75% of the NDCG loss for MLP-INT8. Long queries are stable.
chandra: any evidence this is tokenization vs scoring noise?
alicia: did two checks: 1) re-run MLP-INT8 with `context_padding=12` (previously 2) - short-query NDCG loss reduced by ~0.6pp. 2) canonicalized docs (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) - that also reduced the gap but didn't eliminate it.
sam: sounds like a mix of preproc fragility + numerical dispersion in logits. Do we have per-query paired deltas?
alicia: yes, I computed per-query delta = ndcg10_quant - ndcg10_fp. Distribution is heavy-right (many zeros/tiny gains) with a long left tail. Fraction worse (ndcg decrease > 0.01) for MLP-INT8 on short queries = 18%, fraction better = 9%.
david: how about rank-instability metric?
alicia: I added "rank_instability" = fraction of queries with any change in top10 ordering. Results:
  - full-FP vs MLP-INT8: rank_instability = 22% (short-query = 31%)
  - full-FP vs ATT-INT8: rank_instability = 14% (short-query = 18%)
fiona: top-1 changes? critical for UX.
alicia: top1 change fraction tiny: 1.3% (MLP-INT8). Mostly swaps around positions 4-8.
chandra: can you paste the eval command and candidate pool size you used?
alicia: sure, command used (k=100 candidates):
```
python -m eval.run \
  --model rf-7b-v2 \
  --variants full_fp,mlp_int8,att_int8 \
  --holdout prod_holdout \
  --candidates_k 100 \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10,rank_instability \
  --slices short_query,long_query \
  --seed 2026 \
  --paired_bootstrap 2000
```
sam: candidate beam could matter if quant affects score spread. Try k=200? Also run with 3 different seeds to check stochasticity.
alicia: queued those. I also started a run that quantizes only the final linear (head) to see sensitivity.

alicia: small failure examples (short queries) where ordering flipped unfavorably for MLP-INT8:
  1) query: "install docker"
     - FP top3: [docA (rel=1.0), docB (0.87), docC (0.82)]
     - MLP-INT8 top3: [docA, docC, docB]  # docB/ docC swapped, human preference favors docB
  2) query: "python http server"
     - FP ranks: docX, docY, docZ
     - MLP-INT8: docY moved up, docX demoted to 3

alicia: inspection of logits shows score gaps shrink in MLP-INT8 (e.g., top3 logits: [5.02, 4.96, 4.88] -> [4.98, 4.90, 4.92]) which can flip ordering.
david: that supports the numeric-dispersion hypothesis. Could do temperature scaling on scores before softmax or re-rank with a tiny isotropic calibration offset.
chandra: or use mixed precision: keep MLP layers in FP16 for short-query-heavy pools, allow MLP-INT8 elsewhere.
sam: ops question: is MLP-INT8 necessary for target perf/cost? How much gain?
alicia: latency down ~18% and GPU memory use down ~12% on our dedicated infra for MLP-INT8 vs full-FP. ATT-INT8 gives ~9% latency improvement. So MLP-INT8 is highest win.
fiona: tradeoff: 18% latency vs 1.5% NDCG drop concentrated in short queries. Product decision depends on tolerance.
david: proposed mitigations to test next: 1) score calibration post-quant (linear rescale learned on small dev set), 2) per-slice fallback policy (short-query -> FP model), 3) hybrid: MLP-INT8 + 1-step float rescoring for top10 candidates.
alicia: I'll run linear rescale fit on a held-out dev slice and run the rescoring hack (compute scores int8, select top20, recompute scores with FP head).
chandra: please include per-query example list and confusion-rate (how often FP rank within top10 contains the human-best doc and quant variant doesn't).
alicia: will add. Also documenting seeds and raw diffs to S3: s3://redwood-results/rerank/6173467890/ (raw CSVs + failure examples).
sam: thanks. I'm leaning towards shipping MLP-INT8 to dedicated but gating short-query sensitive routes until we validate rescoring mitigations.
fiona: agree. If rescoring closes >70% of failures we can enable with canary.
alicia: action items: 1) run k=200 + 3 seeds (alicia), 2) run rescoring top20 FP-head (alicia), 3) try linear calibration (david), 4) prepare small human review set of 200 short queries (fiona) for sanity check. I'll post follow-ups in this thread.
